title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.16). X is a compact connected Riemann surface of genus g >= 2, x a base point, pi = pi_1(X,x), and H = PGL(2,C). M^phi(X) is the moduli of flat projective-line bundles on X without automorphisms, a smooth space of complex dimension 6g-6. Via monodromy it is identified with Hom^!(pi,H)/H, the representations with trivial stabiliser modulo conjugation. Points of Hom^! are interpreted geometrically as flat P^1-bundles P together with an identification phi of the fibre at x with P^1.

(1) Action of the outer automorphism group. Aut(pi) acts on Hom(pi,H) on the right by rho.u = rho o u. This commutes with the conjugation action of H. For u = int(g) one has rho o int(g) = int(rho(g)) o rho. Hence Gamma = Autext(pi) = Aut(pi)/Int(pi) acts on Hom^!(pi,H)/H, and by transport of structure on M^phi(X). Grothendieck asserts, with a marginal '?', that this action is not algebraic. In modern terms: the action is algebraic on the Betti (character-variety) structure, but not on the de Rham algebraic structure that M^phi(X) carries as a moduli space over X. This continues the remark on p.16 that the Riemann-Hilbert identification is only analytic.

(2) Teichmüller space into the character variety. A curve Y of genus g with an exterior isomorphism pi_1(Y) ~ pi is a point of Teichmüller space M_g(pi), rigidified by pi. The uniformisation (Fuchsian) representation rho_Y : pi_1(Y) -> PSL(2,R) inside H, defined up to conjugation, then gives a point of M^phi(X). This yields an injective analytic map T_g -> M^phi(X), equivariant for the Teichmüller modular group Gamma. Grothendieck expects the image to be closed but not constructible; indeed it is a totally real, real-analytic submanifold of half dimension. He describes the image as the injective rho admitting a connected invariant domain D in P^1(C), 'which will be unique', on which pi acts freely with compact quotient.

(3) Monodromy of projective connections. M_conn(X) is the space of projective connections (projective structures) on the fixed curve X. Realised as P^1-bundles with a distinguished section and a flat connection, it is a torsor under H^0(X, omega^{⊗2}), of dimension 3g-3. Monodromy gives M_conn(X) -> M^phi(X), a morphism of algebraic schemes for the de Rham structure. Grothendieck asks whether it is injective, i.e. whether two distinct projective connections on X can give isomorphic flat P^1-bundles.

(4) Automorphisms of the Gunning bundle. He studies the underlying bundle P = P(P^1_{X/S}(omega)), the projectivised bundle of first-order principal parts. Up to twist it is the non-split extension 0 -> omega -> E -> O_X -> 0, i.e. the Gunning (uniformisation) bundle.
- An automorphism of P(E) comes from an isomorphism E ~ E ⊗ L. Taking determinants gives L^2 ~ O_X.
- Composing omega -> E -> L gives a section of omega^{-1} ⊗ L. This vanishes because the degree is negative (the line bundle is anti-ample, as the next page says).
- Hence the destabilising sub-line-bundle omega, i.e. the section sigma, is preserved by every automorphism.

The next page completes the computation:
- L ~ O_X.
- The scalar lambda on omega satisfies lambda*c = c, where c ≠ 0 in H^1(omega) is the extension class, so lambda = 1.
- Hence Aut_X(P) = Aut_X(P, sigma) ~ H^0(X, omega), acting by unipotent extension automorphisms.

The remaining question is whether some u_omega can carry the horizontal-section curve C of one projective connection onto that of another. This is the oper-style proof that the monodromy map from projective structures on a fixed X is injective.
errors: The claim that the Out(pi) action is 'not algebraic' needs qualifying (Grothendieck flags it with '?'). On Hom(pi,H)/H with its natural representation-variety structure the action is algebraic; it is non-algebraic only for the de Rham structure coming from X.

The characterisation of the image of Teichmüller space is inaccurate. Injective rho with a connected invariant domain D, free action and compact quotient D/pi describe quasi-Fuchsian groups, an open set, not the closed Fuchsian locus. Moreover D is not unique: a Fuchsian group has two invariant discs, and a quasi-Fuchsian group two invariant components.

The modular group acting holomorphically on Teichmüller space is Out^+(pi), the orientation-preserving part. The full Aut(pi)/Int(pi) includes orientation-reversing classes that act anti-holomorphically and exchange the two orientations of the Fuchsian holonomy.
The notation M_g^Gamma(X) on this page should match M^phi(X) of the previous page; the superscript drifts in the manuscript.

ideas.what: Action of Out(pi_1) on the PGL2(C) character variety by precomposition, transported to the de Rham moduli of flat P^1-bundles, and its non-algebraicity there
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group action on Betti moduli vs de Rham moduli; non-algebraicity of the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; systematised by Simpson (Betti/de Rham/Dolbeault moduli, 1990s); Goldman for the dynamics

ideas.what: Teichmüller space as curves with an exterior isomorphism of pi_1 with a fixed pi, mapped injectively and equivariantly into the PGL2 character variety by uniformising holonomy; image closed but not algebraically constructible
ideas.modern_name: Fuchsian locus / Teichmüller component in the character variety
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Henri Cartan 1960/61 (Teichmüller theory talks), for the rigidification by pi_1; the holonomy embedding itself unsure

ideas.what: Projective connections on fixed X form an H^0(omega^2)-torsor, with an algebraic monodromy map to the moduli of flat P^1-bundles; question of injectivity
ideas.modern_name: Holonomy map of complex projective structures on a fixed Riemann surface (injective; proper embedding)

ideas.what: Automorphisms of the Gunning bundle P(J^1 omega): any automorphism preserves the distinguished section (Hom(omega, L ⊗ ... ) = 0 by negativity), and Aut_X(P) ~ H^0(X, omega)
ideas.modern_name: Opers have no automorphisms / uniqueness of the oper flag (Borel reduction) on the Gunning bundle

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats projective structures as P^1-bundles with a section, i.e. as PGL2-opers. He computes the automorphism group of the Gunning bundle in order to prove injectivity of the monodromy map from projective structures. This is algebraic, oper-style reasoning predating Beilinson-Drinfeld's formalism, but both the results and the method are now standard.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck working through uniformisation and projective structures algebraically. No new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard material: character varieties, the Out(pi) action, Fuchsian holonomy of Teichmüller space, the projective-structure monodromy map and Gunning-bundle automorphisms. It is all well known (Gunning, Hejhal, Goldman, Beilinson-Drinfeld). The interest is historical: Grothendieck's algebraic oper-like treatment and his awareness of the de Rham/Betti non-algebraicity. There are also small errors in describing the Fuchsian image.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'φ : P^1(C) → P^1_R' is more plausibly an isomorphism between the fibre P_x at the base point and P^1(C) (rigidification at x), not a map to P^1_R.
The relation should read ρ ∘ int(g) = int(ρ(g)) ∘ ρ, not '... ∘ u'.
'M_g^Γ(X)' is the same space as M^φ(X) of the previous page (flat P^1-bundle moduli); the Γ superscript is likely a misreading of φ.
'le groupe [?] qui [?] : Hom^!(π,H)/H' likely reads 'le groupe qui opère sur Hom^!(π,H)/H, c'est Γ = Autext(π)'.
'C'est un fibré [?] sur le contenu [?] de dim finie H^0(X, Ω^{⊗2})' likely reads 'C'est un fibré principal (torseur) sous le vectoriel de dim finie H^0(X, Ω^{⊗2})'.
'P^1_{X/S}(ω)' denotes the sheaf of first-order principal parts (jets) of ω.
